messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's Py SDK 0.18.0 release we saw quota attributions flip to the wrong tenant for ~0.2% of requests in staging. Repro attached. It looks like the new `x-redwood-route` header rename changed casing/namespace handling and our console's legacy parser is ignoring it. Example request:
```http
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Route: tenant=acct-123;route=beta
Authorization: Bearer ...
```
Now the SDK sends `X-Redwood-Route: tenant=acct-123;route=beta` and the console's legacy parser lowercases header names and falls back to a different parse path that doesn't recognize `x-redwood-route`. Result: some requests are attributed to the wrong tenant. Can we avoid charging wrong quotas in prod?

kevin: Any logs with request ids? Is this only Python or also Go/TS?

maria: Repro logs: TRACE ids 0a1b2c..ff show both Py and Go clients affected in staging. TS clients still emit `x-route` (legacy) so they weren't impacted.

jonathan: We should do a two-pronged approach: (1) console parser accept both new and legacy headers (case-insensitive) and dedupe; (2) SDKs ship a short-lived opt-in shim that sends the legacy header in addition to the new header while teams migrate. UX wise, we should avoid any automatic opt-in.

carla: Agree. Fast fix on console side: adjust header canonicalization and prefer `x-redwood-route` when both present. We'll also dedupe by header value so metrics/quotas don't double count. I'll open a parser PR and push to canary region A.

kevin: For SDKs, propose we add a flag `send_legacy_route_header` default false. For a migration window we can publish a minor patch that defaults to false and recommend customers enable it temporarily. Example (Py):
```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=..., send_legacy_route_header=True)
```
But note: duplication of routing info could be considered sensitive in some deployments; check with security.

maria: Route header doesn't contain secrets but double-reporting is the main concern. Console dedupe will handle it. Also, the proxy update that changed casing appears to have rolled out last night which triggered this.

alex: FYI I pinged infra/proxy team — they rolled a change that normalized header casing to Title-Case which exposed this mismatch. They're prepared to rollback if needed.

carla: PR #3421 created: parser now accepts `x-route`, `x-Redwood-route`, and `x-redwood-route` case-insensitively, and dedupes identical values. Rolling to canary (region-a) now.

sdk-bot: deploybot: canary deploy started for console parser patch to region-a (build 2026.03.12-3421).

jonathan: For rollout UX: add a console banner for org admins when we detect mixed header types and a dashboard widget that shows percent legacy vs new over last 24h (query: `count(where header_type='legacy') / count(*)`). Helps customers understand when to flip the flag in SDKs.

kevin: Plan for SDKs: Py 0.18.1 (opt-in flag), Go 0.9.3 (opt-in flag), TS patch with a docs note (TS already emits legacy header). I'll own Py & Go changelog entries. Schedule: cut tomorrow AM, coordinate with canary console window.

maria: I'll monitor staging for 4 hours after canary and alert on >0.1% misattribution. If we see regression, we'll revert Py release and roll back proxy change.

kevin: TODOs: (1) carla -> console PR #3421 (canary) (2) kevin -> Py/Go opt-in patch + release notes (3) jonathan -> add banner + dashboard query (4) maria -> staging monitor & rollback threshold. Assigning owners in the ticket.

maria: Thanks team. @alex please keep me posted if proxy rollback happens.

alex: Will do.

kevin: quick Q: should we send both headers by default for internal infra customers? I'm leaning no — avoid surprises. Opt-in only and recommend 2-week transition window.

carla: +1 opt-in only. We'll instrument an alert if we see conflicting headers beyond a threshold so we can nudge opt-in usage.

maria: :thumbsup:
